title: Millisecond-path profiling for token-level cost & cache-impact
creator: Asha Patel
description: Add a low-overhead profiling pipeline that emits millisecond-resolution spans for each token processing step so we can attribute latency and estimated cost at token granularity and measure how KV cache hits/misses change per-token latency. The goal is to enable per-model and per-route dashboards that show token latency distributions, cumulative cost by token position, and the delta introduced by cache misses so engineering and SRE can tune batching, cache policies, and kernel selection.
acceptance_criteria: Runtime emits per-token span events (token_index, stage, ms) for production traffic with sampling config and without emitting token plaintext
Aggregator reconstructs ordered per-request token timelines and stores aggregated summaries to metrics and compressed logs within budgeted storage (<0.5% increase in observability ingestion),
Dashboard shows per-model 50/90/99 token-latency percentiles, cache_hit vs cache_miss delta curves, and per-route cost-per-token estimates updated hourly
End-to-end overhead on tail latency for a 4k token request < 1% p99 compared to baseline, proven in canary rollout
Automated tests for span emission, ordering correctness, and privacy safeguards (no prompt text persisted)
Playbook entry created for investigating token-level regressions with example queries and runbook steps
implementation_notes: Instrument runtime paths to emit lightweight spans for stages: tokenizer, prefix-cache-lookup, batch-dispatch, kernel-exec, kv-write, post-process
Use a compact protobuf schema for spans with token_index (int), stage (enum), duration_ms (int), cache_hit (bool, optional), model_id, request_id, batch_id
Span emission must avoid copying token text: only include token_hash and token_index. Hashing done with SHA256 truncated to 8 bytes to preserve privacy while enabling dedup and joins
Add sampling policy: default 0.5% sampling globally, 5% for routes flagged as heavy; provide dynamic sampling config from console

Aggregator service collates spans per request_id and writes two artifacts: summarized metrics (Prometheus-compatible counters/histograms) and compressed ordered logs (gzip+snappy) for forensic queries
Backpressure: span emitter should be best-effort with a fixed-size ring buffer and drop-on-full signal metric; ensure emitter is non-blocking to avoid affecting runtime latency
Privacy/security: disallow token-text fields through linting and CI checks; require security sign-off if security_review_required toggled
Rollout plan: feature flag gated by customer tier and region, staged canary on 1% of traffic then 10% then 100% with monitoring thresholds for increased ingress and tail latency
progress_updates: 2025-02-18: Spike complete. PoC implemented to emit per-token spans from the continuous-batching loop. Measured ~0.3% overhead on p50 and ~0.8% on p99 for sampled traffic.

2025-02-25: Aggregator prototype added to observability worker; can reconstruct ordering for batched requests using request_id+batch_id. First end-to-end run produced expected per-token latency curves for a small test workload.
2025-02-28: Privacy review checklist applied. Replaced token text with 8-byte truncated SHA256 token_hash. CI lint rule prevents token_text fields in span schema.
2025-03-02: Dashboard wireframes reviewed with PM and SRE. Decided on position_bucket sizes [1,2-8,9-64,65-512,>512] for visualization performance.
2025-03-04: Submitted runtime PR for non-blocking span emitter and sampling config. Open PR: runtime change and protobuf schema extension awaiting code review. Canaries scheduled after merge.
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Additional observability ingress could increase costs and SLO risk. Mitigation: aggressive sampling and position bucketing to reduce cardinality; compressed logs for forensic use.
Risk: Wrong ordering reconstruction for heavily-batched requests. Mitigation: include batch_seq and batch_len in spans and validate ordering in aggregator with unit tests and property checks.
Risk: accidental exposure of prompt data. Mitigation: schema linting in CI, code review checklist, and automated redaction tests that run on PRs touching span emission codepaths.
qa_plan: Create synthetic workloads with deterministic token timings to validate aggregator ordering and per-stage sums match runtime timers
Run end-to-end canary with 1% traffic and verify p99 tail before/after on representative endpoints
Load test observability ingest path with expected production sampling rates to validate storage and query latency
Security QA: run the redaction fuzzer to ensure no token text persists in stored artifacts
